title: Sable and the Visitor
premise: August Lockridge, a late-night radio host grieving his sister's death, begins receiving calls from listeners who died the previous week — including, eventually, his sister. The calls are tied to an old frost-patterned mirror in his inherited house, which reflects each room one second behind reality, and behind that delay something is listening back. As August investigates what his family invited in decades ago to save his dying mother, he must choose between exposing the truth (which will free the trapped dead but destroy his name and career) or staying silent until sunrise, when the frost completes its final pattern and claims him as the next voice on the line. He chooses truth at dawn, speaking his sister's story live on air; the mirror shatters, the dead go quiet, but the final call comes from a listener who hasn't died yet.
about_author: Astrid Reyes is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent six years answering calls from strangers in the dark before turning to horror fiction. She writes from a farmhouse in northern Vermont, where she keeps every mirror in the house covered after sundown.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV August. On the anniversary week of his sister Wren's death, August hosts 'The Night Line,' mocking a caller who claims the dead are phoning in. He signs off at 4 a.m., alone in the house he inherited. Emotional beat: brittle denial wrapped in professional charm.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: POV August. Sorting Wren's belongings, August finds her note: 'Don't answer after three.' He laughs it off, but pockets the house key she wore as a necklace. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through irritation.

chapters.title: First Call
chapters.summary: POV August. A caller named Denny asks about a debt he owed before dying last Tuesday. August checks the obituary mid-broadcast. The line goes dead; so does the studio clock. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in disbelief.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV August. Home at dawn, August notices his bathroom mirror lags — his reflection blinks after he does. He blames exhaustion. Emotional beat: uncanny dread rationalized away.

chapters.title: Frost in July
chapters.summary: POV August. Frost creeps across the hallway mirror in fern patterns despite summer heat. Under it, faintly, handwriting. Emotional beat: the house stops being neutral ground.

chapters.title: Denny's Debt
chapters.summary: POV August. Denny calls again, desperate: 'It only gets one chance to ask you right.' He names the hallway mirror before hanging up. August drives to the station rather than sleep. Emotional beat: fear converting into investigation.

chapters.title: Wren's Notebook
chapters.summary: POV August. In Wren's locked desk, August finds research on their grandmother's séance circle and a photograph of the mirror being carried into the house in 1971. Emotional beat: the past has teeth.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: POV August. On air, a woman calls asking whether her husband suffered. August recognizes her voice from a funeral notice. She says, 'He's standing behind you,' and the studio door opens onto darkness. Emotional beat: terror with no exit.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: POV Mara Voss, a skeptical parapsychologist who once debunked August on air, arrives uninvited after hearing the broadcast. She brings instruments and old contempt. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared unease.

chapters.title: What the Meters Say
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Her equipment records a voice repeating August's childhood nickname in the empty hallway. Mara, professionally ruined by one earlier hoax, refuses to publish what she's seeing. Emotional beat: loyalty to truth warring with self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Séance Tapes
chapters.summary: POV August. Reel-to-reel tapes in the attic capture grandmother Edith's circle begging 'the Quiet Guest' to heal their dying mother. It agreed — for a pattern of voices, one per generation. Emotional beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Mother's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV August. Hospital records confirm: Edith's mother recovered impossibly in 1971. The price was never paid forward. Wren was supposed to be the voice. Emotional beat: love weaponized across generations.

chapters.title: Wren Calls
chapters.summary: POV August. At 3:07 a.m., Wren's voice on the night line: 'Augie, don't let it finish the pattern.' Static swallows her mid-sentence. Emotional beat: hope and heartbreak in one breath.

chapters.title: Covered Glass
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara covers every mirror with black cloth; the frost blooms on windows instead, spelling half a word. They realize the house itself is becoming the mirror. Emotional beat: the trap is larger than they thought.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV August. Elderly neighbor Ruthie recalls the 1971 winter: seven families lost someone the week the mirror arrived. 'Your grandma bought spring with other people's winters.' Emotional beat: the town's complicity surfaces.

chapters.title: Seven Names
chapters.summary: POV August. August cross-references Ruthie's memory with archives: seven deaths, seven voices owed. Six were taken over decades. One slot remains open — and it has his name penciled beside it. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of doom.

chapters.title: Mara's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara admits her career-ending 'hoax' was real phenomena she falsified data against out of fear. She owes the truth to someone; maybe to August. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Delay Grows
chapters.summary: POV August. The mirror now lags two seconds. In the gap, August sees himself turn toward something he cannot see directly. Emotional beat: being watched by your own life.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: POV August. The radio broadcasts without power — Wren's show, a recording that never existed, interviewing guests who died this week. The Quiet Guest is learning the format. Emotional beat: horror wearing familiarity.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Warning
chapters.summary: POV August. Ruthie, found frozen in her July kitchen, left a note: 'It can't take what's freely given. Don't let it take you free.' Contradiction or clue? Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Pattern Completes
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The frost finishes its design: a perfect ring of seven ferns, six blackened, one pale and waiting. Sunrise is forty hours out. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: Calling the Dead
chapters.summary: POV August. August deliberately opens the lines, inviting the dead callers to speak their unfinished business on record. Denny confesses his debt; the widow forgives her husband aloud. Each voice frees a fern. Emotional beat: justice outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Station Siege
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The Quiet Guest follows the signal to the station; temperatures plummet, staff flee, and the transmitter burns cold instead of hot. Mara stays at the board. Emotional beat: loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: Edith Speaks
chapters.summary: POV August. Through the dead frequency, grandmother Edith's voice returns: instructions for unbinding the bargain — the seventh voice must be given willingly, witnessed, and named. Emotional beat: ancestral amends.

chapters.title: What Wren Knew
chapters.summary: POV August. Wren's hidden letter reveals she discovered the bargain weeks before her 'accident' and chose silence to protect August. His rage at her secrecy curdles into understanding. Emotional beat: love against duty, fully priced.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV August. The Quiet Guest speaks directly at last, through every reflective surface: give your voice freely and Wren returns for one year. Emotional beat: temptation engineered from grief.

chapters.title: Mara's Stand
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara threatens to broadcast everything — the bargain, the seven names, the town's debt — unless the Guest honors its own rules. Truth as a weapon. Emotional beat: courage born of past cowardice.

chapters.title: Blackout
chapters.summary: POV August. Power fails town-wide; the Guest isolates the house. August and Mara work by candlelight, splicing Edith's tapes into a counter-broadcast. Emotional beat: two people against the dark, hand in hand.

chapters.title: The Uninvited Hour
chapters.summary: POV August. 3 a.m. The mirrors all reflect rooms that aren't there — 1971, the séance, his mother's sickbed. August walks into the reflection physically. Emotional beat: crossing the threshold.

chapters.title: Inside the Glass
chapters.summary: POV August. Within the delayed world, August meets the six taken voices and Wren, flickering. The Guest appears as a patient figure made of frost-ferns, courteous, ancient, starving. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion entwined.

chapters.title: The Guest's Hunger
chapters.summary: POV August. The Guest explains: it was invited, bound, and then forgotten — owed warmth for fifty years. Its grievance is almost just. Emotional beat: sympathy for the monster complicating everything.

chapters.title: Mara on Air
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Running the transmitter on generator power, Mara broadcasts the whole truth to the sleeping town: names, dates, the bargain. Listeners wake and speak forgiveness into their phones. Emotional beat: collective witness as exorcism.

chapters.title: The Sixth Fern
chapters.summary: POV August. As the town's words reach the glass, the sixth fern ignites white. The Guest weakens; Wren solidifies enough to touch August's hand. Emotional beat: love literally warming the dead.

chapters.title: Bargain Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV August. August offers a new contract: not a voice taken, but stories told freely — a nightly hour where the living speak for the dead, willingly, forever. The Guest hesitates. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Sunrise Terms
chapters.summary: POV August and Mara alternating. With minutes to dawn, the Guest demands a guarantor. Mara signs herself in as keeper of the broadcast hour. August protests; she refuses to yield. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen, not stolen.

chapters.title: The Shattering
chapters.summary: POV August. At first light August speaks Wren's full story live, naming every wrong and every love. The mirror bursts; frost evaporates; the dead callers sign off one by one, grateful. Emotional beat: catharsis through truth-telling.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: POV August. Days later: Wren is gone properly now, at peace. The house is warm. August sleeps without dreams for the first time in the book. Emotional beat: exhausted, earned quiet.

chapters.title: The Night Line, Reborn
chapters.summary: POV August. August reopens the show as 'The Long Hour' — listeners call in memories of their dead, and somewhere Mara keeps the promise. Ratings soar; the dead stay quiet. Emotional beat: purpose rebuilt from ruin.

chapters.title: One Last Call
chapters.summary: POV August. Final segment, 3:07 a.m.: a caller with a living voice asks whether the show takes requests. August checks his log — the man isn't scheduled to die until next week. Emotional beat: chill of continuation.

chapters.title: Sable and the Visitor
chapters.summary: POV August. August answers anyway: 'Tell me what you need said.' The frost ferns on the window bloom white instead of black — listening, perhaps, but held to terms. He holds out until sunrise, again. Emotional beat: vigilance as devotion; the ending as beginning.
